Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:10:1.hebrew: מנין לתמורת פסולי המוקדשים שמתה - כגון דלאחר שנפדו הקדשים התפיסן בתמורה, דלא מצו למיקרב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:10:1.english: From where [is it derived] that the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals dies - For example, where after the consecrated animals were redeemed, one designated [animals] as a substitute for them, since they cannot be offered:

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:10:2.hebrew: ממעלה הגרה טמא הוא - דסיפיה דקרא כתיב: "טמא הוא לכם", ודרשינן הכי: יש לך דבר שיש בו סימני טהרה ואסור באכילה, ואיזו זו? תמורת פסולי המוקדשין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:10:2.english: Of them that chew the cud, it is impure - For at the end of the verse it is written: “It is impure to you,” and we expound thus: You have an item that possesses signs of purity and [yet] is forbidden for consumption, and which is this? The substitute of disqualified consecrated [animals].

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:10:3.english: Five sin offerings - [This] is explained in [tractate] Temurah (daf 21b).

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:11:1.hebrew: לתמורת אשם - שתהא רועה, דאשם לא קרב נדבה, הלכך תמורתו לא קרבה. והא טמא דקרא, ה"ק: הניחוהו עד שיהא טמא, כלומר שיפול בו מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:11:1.english: For the substitute of a guilt offering - That it shall graze, for a guilt offering is not sacrificed as a voluntary offering; therefore, its substitute is not sacrificed [either]. And this [word] "impure" in the verse, this is what it is saying: Leave it until it becomes impure — that is to say, that a blemish should fall upon it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:12:1.english: In any [case] where a sin offering [is left to] die - And the substitute of a sin offering is one of the five sin offerings [that are left to] die.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:13:1.english: There is no negative commandment - That he does not transgress a negative commandment.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:13:2.english: That there is a negative mitzva - [As the verse states:] “You shall not eat of them that chew the cud” (Leviticus 11:4).

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:14:1.hebrew: ואבע"א - להכי אתא ממפריסי הפרסה, דמשתעי בחטאות המתות, להקיש דבר הבא ממעלי הגרה — תמורת פסולי המוקדשין לאחר פדיונן, דנפקא ממעלי הגרה — לדבר הבא ממפריסי הפרסה — חטאות המתות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:14:1.english: And if you wish, say - For this [purpose] did [the phrase] “of them that have a split hoof” come, which speaks of the sin offerings [left] to die — to juxtapose an item that comes from “those that chew the cud” — [namely,] the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption, which is derived from “those that chew the cud” — with an item that comes from “those that have a split hoof” — [namely,] the sin offerings [left] to die.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:15:1.hebrew: המקבל צאן ברזל - ששם לו עובד כוכבים בהמותיו בדמים קצובין, ולתת לו אותן דמים עד עשר שנים — בין מתו בין הוזלו — ואותן ולדות שיהיו להן עד אותו זמן, יהיו ביניהם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:15:1.english: One who receives a guaranteed investment - Where a gentile appraised his animals to him at a fixed value, and [the recipient is] to give him that money within ten years — whether they died or depreciated — and those offspring that they will have until that time will be [divided] between them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:1:1.hebrew: לאתויי חלבו - דאסור. ולאתויי שוחטו בחוץ דחייב לא אמרינן, משום דא"כ איבעי לן למימר בדוקין שבעין, ועוד, סיפא קתני לקמן: השוחטן בחוץ פטור. וכללא דרישא לא אצטריך לאיתויי חלבו דשרי, דהשתא ולדן דכגופן דמי — דעובר ירך אמו הוא — שרי, כל שכן חלבו, דמיא בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:1:1.english: To include its milk - That it is forbidden [to consume]. And to include one who slaughters it outside, that he is liable [to karet] — we do not say [this], because if so, we would have needed to state [that it refers to an animal] with cataracts in the eye; and furthermore, the latter clause teaches below: "One who slaughters them outside is exempt." And the general rule of the first clause was not needed to include its milk, that it is permitted, for now, [since] their offspring, which is considered like their [own] body — as a fetus is [considered] a thigh of its mother — is permitted, all the more so its milk, which is merely [bodily] fluid.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:2:1.hebrew: הא בעלי מומין מיפרקי - אותם שנתעברו קודם פדיון ונולדו לאחר פדיון, וכגון שתפסן לשום זבח, דאלימא קדושתייהו למיתפס פדיונן; וכשהוא מתפיסן לשם זבח — אין מתפיסן לכל זבח שירצה, הא לשם אותו זבח מתפיסן. "והיכי משכחת לה" — פירושא הוא, כלומר: היכי משכחת תירוצא דמילתא? דמשמע: בעלי מומין נפדין, ולשם זבח אחר לא יתפיסם; אלא היכי עביד? דמתפיסם לשם אותו הזבח, ונפדין במומן כשיפול בהן מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:2:1.english: Which indicates that blemished [offspring] may be redeemed - [This refers to] those that were conceived before redemption and born after redemption, and where he dedicated them as an offering, so that their sanctity is powerful [enough] for their redemption to take effect; and when he dedicates them as an offering, he may not dedicate them as any offering he desires, but rather as that [same] offering he may dedicate them. And [the phrase] "How can you find it?" is an explanation; that is to say: How can you find a resolution to the matter? For [the baraita] implies [that] blemished [offspring] are redeemed, and for another offering he may not dedicate them; rather, how does he act? By dedicating them as that same offering, and they are redeemed with their blemish when a blemish falls upon them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:3:1.hebrew: נימא תהוי תיובתא דרב הונא - דאמר לעיל: כונסן לכיפה, והן מתים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:3:1.english: Shall we say that this is a refutation of Rav Huna - For he said earlier: One gathers them into a chamber, and they die.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:4:1.hebrew: ואיידי דתני רישא נפדין תמימים - דחידוש הוא, דאפילו תמימים נפדים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:4:1.english: And since the first clause taught: They are redeemed unblemished - For it is a novel ruling that even unblemished [animals] are redeemed:

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:1.hebrew: והשוחטן בחוץ פטור - סיפא דברייתא לעיל, אקדשים שקדם הקדשן את מומן קאי. ואפילו הכי פטור, דאין חייבין על שחיטת חוץ אלא על המתקבל בפנים, כדתנן בזבחים בפרק פרת חטאת (זבחים דף קיב.): בעלי מומין, בין קבועין בין עוברין, שהקריבן בחוץ — פטור. ומפיק טעמא מהאי קרא: "ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו" — הא כל שאינו ראוי לבא אל פתח אהל מועד, אין חייבין עליו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:1.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt - The latter clause of the baraita above refers to consecrated animals whose consecration preceded their blemish. And even so, he is exempt, for one is liable for slaughter outside [the Temple courtyard] only for [that which] is acceptable inside, as we learned in a mishna in Zevachim in the chapter [entitled] Parat Chatat (Zevachim 112b): Blemished animals, whether [with] permanent [blemishes] or transient [blemishes], one who offered them outside is exempt. And it derives the reason from this verse: "And has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" — meaning, for anything that is not fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, one is not liable.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:2.hebrew: רב הונא מתני חייב - כדקתני מתני':
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:2.english: Rav Huna taught: [He is] liable - As the Mishnah teaches.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:3.english: And he interprets it [as referring to] cataracts in the eye - For it is acceptable inside [the Temple].

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:4.hebrew: ואליבא דרבי עקיבא דאמר - בשחיטת קדשים, בפ' המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פד.): אם עלו לא ירדו. דוקין — טיל"א, כגון (ישעיהו מ) "הנוטה כדוק שמים". ולהכי לא ירדו — דאין מומן ניכר כל כך. הכי תנן בזבחים, בפ' המזבח מקדש הראוי לו (דף פד.): ר' עקיבא מכשיר בבעלי מומין — כלומר, דאם עלו לא ירדו. ואמר רבי יוחנן בגמ': לא הכשיר רבי עקיבא אלא בדוקין שבעין, הואיל וכשירין בעופות, והוא שקדם הקדישן את מומן. ל"א: דוקין — שיש לו מום בעפעפים. ולהכי קרי לעפעפים "דוק" — על העין כרקיע, דהכי אמרינן בספרי אגודות: העין דומה לעולם קטן: העפעפים כנגד הרקיע, והתחתון כנגד הארץ, והלבן שמקיף את העין כנגד ים אוקיינוס שסובב את העולם, והשחור שבו, שהוא עגול, דומה לגלגל חמה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:5:4.english: And in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva, who says: - In [tractate] Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim], in the chapter [entitled] Hamizbe’ach Mekaddesh (Zevachim 84a): If they ascended [the altar], they shall not descend. Dukin [means] toile [a film], as in (Isaiah 40[:22]): “Who stretches out the heavens like a curtain [kedok].” And for this reason they do not descend [from the altar], because their blemish is not so noticeable. So we learned in the Mishnah in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] Hamizbe’ach Mekaddesh HaRa’ui Lo (84a): “Rabbi Akiva deems valid [sacrifices of certain] blemished animals” — that is to say, that if they ascended, they shall not descend. And Rabbi Yochanan said in the Gemara: Rabbi Akiva deemed valid only [animals with] blemishes on the cornea of the eye [dukin sheba’ayin], since [such animals] are valid in the case of birds, and provided that their consecration preceded their blemish. Another explanation: Dukin [means] that it has a blemish on the eyelids. And for this reason [the eyelid] is called dok, [spreading] over the eye like the firmament, for so we say in the books of Aggadah: The eye resembles a miniature world: the eyelids correspond to the firmament and the lower [lid] corresponds to the earth, and the white that surrounds the eye corresponds to the Ocean that encircles the world, and the black [part] within it, which is round, resembles the orb of the sun.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:6:1.english: Deferred sanctity - For they have already been redeemed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:7:1.hebrew: ויאכלו במומן - ימתינו עד שיוממו, ויאכלו לבעלים, כבכור ומעשר שאין נפדין אלא נאכלין במומן. אלמא, כיון דלא מצי קרבי — כדאמר במס' תמורה (דף ה: ע"ש): "אך בכור שור וגו' הן קריבין ואין תמורתן קריבין" — נאכלין במומן לבעלים, הכי נמי ליעבד הכי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:7:1.english: And they are eaten in their blemished state - They must wait until they become blemished and be eaten by the owners, like a firstborn and [an animal] tithe, which are not redeemed, but rather are eaten in their blemished state. Evidently, since they cannot be offered [on the altar] — as [the Gemara] says in Tractate Temurah (5b, see there): "Howbeit the firstling of a bullock, etc." [teaching that] they are offered, but their substitutes are not offered — [yet] they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners, here too, let us do the same.

Rashi on Bekhorot 16a:9:1.english: And this animal is not strong [enough] to take hold of its redemption - Therefore, it must die.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:10:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר ממעלי הגרה - והא דדרשינן בפ"ק (לעיל בכורות דף ו.): "יש לך דבר שהוא מעלה גרה ואי אתה אוכלו, כגון טהור שנולד מן הטמא" — התם דריש מרישיה דקרא: "ואת אלה לא תאכלו", והכא דריש מסיפיה דקרא: "טמא הוא לכם". אי נמי: תרי קראי כתיבי:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:10:1.english: "The verse states: Of them that chew the cud" - And as for that which we expound in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 6a): "You have [an animal] that chews the cud, yet you may not eat it, such as a kosher [animal] that was born from a non-kosher [animal]" — there, it expounds [it] from the beginning of the verse: "These you shall not eat," whereas here, it expounds [it] from the end of the verse: "It is impure to you." Alternatively, two verses are written [one in Leviticus 11:4 and one in Deuteronomy 14:7].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:11:1.hebrew: אלא כי אתא קרא לתמורת אשם - והכי פירושא דברייתא: "מנין לחמש חטאות מתות, וכנגדן באשם רועה?" ו"טמא הוא" — היינו שירעה עד שיסתאב, כדפירש הקונטרס:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:11:1.english: Rather, when the verse came, [it came] for the substitute of a guilt offering - And this is the explanation of the baraita: "From where [is it derived regarding] the five sin offerings that die, and their counterparts among guilt offerings [that they] graze?" And "it is impure" — that is, that it shall graze until it becomes blemished, as the Kontres [Rashi] explained.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:12:1.hebrew: כל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה - אומר רבינו תם, דרעייה מדרבנן היא. ולפי שתקנו חכמים רעייה — נקט בכל דוכתא: "באשם רועה"; אבל הילכתא הכי איתא מדאורייתא: דכל שבחטאת מתה — באשם קרב עולה, כדאמר בפסחים שילהי (סוף) פרק אלו דברים (פסחים דף עג.): אשם שניתק לרעייה ושחטו — כשר לעולה; ושם פירשתי לה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:12:1.english: "In any [case] where a sin offering [is left to] die, a guilt offering [is left to] graze" - Rabbeinu Tam says that [the requirement of] grazing is rabbinic. And because the Sages instituted grazing, [the Gemara] formulates [the rule] everywhere [as]: "a guilt offering [is left to] graze." But the tradition is by Torah law as follows: that in any [case] where a sin offering [is left to] die, in [the case of] a guilt offering, it is sacrificed as a burnt offering, as [the Gemara] says in Pesachim at the end of the chapter [entitled] Ellu Devarim (Pesachim 73a): "A guilt offering that was relegated to grazing and one slaughtered it is fit as a burnt offering." And there I explained it.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:6:1.hebrew: ותמורה שלאחר פדיונו מתה - ואם תאמר: מאי שנא מולדות דאיעבר ואתיליד לאחר פדיונן, דחשבינן לעיל ולד צבי ואיל? ויש לומר: דולדות אין בהן קדושה אלא מכח אמן, וכיון שנפדית פקעה קדושתו לגמרי כצבי וכאיל; ואע"ג דאיכא איסור גיזה ועבודה, אין כח לאיסור מועט כזה שיחול על ידו קדושה על הולדות. אבל תמורת קדושה (בההיא), וכיון דגלי קרא שחלה על בעלת מום קבוע חלה — ה"ה לאחר פדיונן, אלא דלא קרבה. אבל תמורה דלפני פדיונן קרבה, ועדיפא מולדות דלפני פדיונן, דאיכא מ"ד לעיל לרעייה. וכן מוכח לשון הקונטרס דבסמוך, גבי "מנין לתמורת פסולי המוקדשין שמתה", ופי' רש"י: כגון לאחר פדיונו, דלא מצי למיקרב. והא דאצטריך קרא ד"ממעלי הגרה" בסמוך — ללאו אתא, דמסברא ידענו דלא קרבה, כדאמר רב נחמן הכא; וכה"ג אמר בסמוך גבי חמש חטאות. ועוד יש לפרש: דקרא וסברא צריכי; דאי לאו קרא, הוה אמינא לא קדשה כלל, כצבי ואיל, כולדות דאיעבר ואוליד לאחר פדיונן; ואי לאו סברא, הוה אמינא ירעה, ו"טמא הוא" דקרא — הוי "ימתין עד שיהא טמא ויפול בו מום", כדפי' הקונטרס בסמוך. והא דפריך רב עמרם: "ותיתכיל במומה לבעלים" — אסברא דרב נחמן פריך:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 16a:6:1.english: And its substitute [consecrated] after its redemption dies - And if you say: How is [this] different from offspring that were conceived and born after their redemption, which we considered earlier [to be] like the offspring of a gazelle and a deer? And one can say: Offspring have no sanctity in them except by virtue of their mother, and once she was redeemed, her sanctity ceased entirely, [rendering her] like a gazelle and a deer; and even though there is a prohibition against shearing and work, such a minor prohibition does not have the power to cause sanctity to take effect upon the offspring through it. However, a substitute [receives its] sanctity [(through that)] — and since Scripture revealed that [substitution] takes effect upon [an animal substituted for] a permanently blemished animal, it takes effect; the same applies [even] after their redemption, except that it is not offered [on the altar]. However, a substitute [consecrated] before their redemption is offered, and is superior to offspring [born] before their redemption, regarding which there is an authority earlier who maintains [that they are sent] to pasture. And so is proven by the phrasing of the Kunteres [Rashi] nearby, regarding: "From where is it derived that the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals dies?", and Rashi explained: "For instance, [a substitute consecrated] after its redemption, since it cannot be offered." And that which the verse "of them that chew the cud" is needed nearby — it comes for a negative prohibition [against eating it]; for based on logical reasoning we would know [only] that it is not offered, as Rav Naḥman stated here; and similarly, [the Gemara] states nearby regarding the five sin offerings. And furthermore, one can explain that both the verse and the logical reasoning are necessary: For were it not for the verse, I would have said that it does not become holy at all, [being] like a gazelle and a deer, similar to offspring that were conceived and born after their redemption; and were it not for the logical reasoning, I would have said that it should graze, and "it is impure" in the verse means: "let it wait until it is impure and a blemish falls upon it," as the Kunteres [Rashi] explained nearby. And as for that which Rav Amram objected: "Then let it be eaten in its blemished state by the owners" — he was objecting to the logical reasoning of Rav Naḥman.
